newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill rates higher but not many buyers.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill rates higher but not many buyers.

text.p: Manila banks were quoting higher bid-and-offer rates in the secondary market in line with an expected rise at the T-bill auction later today, traders said.
"Many are selling but no one wants to buy," a trader said.
Another said there was buying of bills from corporate clients but banks were not actively positioning.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave offers of 10.50/10.95 percent for the three-month bills; 11/11.50 percent for six months; and 11.50/11.95 percent for the one year.
"We're expecting a 20 to 30 basis points increase across all tenors in the auction," the trader said.
Banks projected rates to go up after the Central Bank raised its term reverse repo rates on Thursday.
Moreover, they expect Thailand's financial woes to persist, putting pressures on the peso and domestic interest rates.
